item.title: War of words between Michigan Wolverines-Oregon Ducks heats up as Dan Lanning responds to criticisms
item.description: Kyle Whittingham took aim at Oregon's $50M+ NIL spending, and Dan Lanning fired back with a pointed jab at Michigan's costly coaching buyouts.
item.content:encoded:
Well, the Big Ten Conference might not be having the best season on the field, but off the field? The drama just keeps brewing. And of all teams, this time it involves ... the Michigan Wolverines and Oregon Ducks?

The two teams, both having varying degrees of disappointing results thus far in 2026, face off on Saturday in Eugene, and despite the lack of history between the two programs, there's some bad blood rapidly brewing.

It started thanks to already-embattled Michigan head coach Kyle Whittingham. His first season in Ann Arbor has been, to put it mildly, well below expectations. While at Utah, the 66-year-old was known for being a calm, steady voice of leadership who seemed to always win the games he needed to win. The Utes punched well above their historical weight, and his penchant for stability. Whittingham was in Salt Lake City for 32 years, looked like a perfect fit for a Michigan program coming off years of turmoil.

MICHIGAN'S NEW HEAD COACH POURS COLD WATER ON OHIO STATE RIVALRY: 'HATE IS A STRONG WORD'

But the Wolverines' struggles started almost immediately. Whittingham dismissed the importance of the Michigan-Ohio State rivalry game, which put him on the wrong foot with most fans. Then the Wolverines required some questionable clock management from the replay review crew to pull out a miraculous 13-12 comeback win over Western Michigan. They rebounded to beat Oklahoma the following week, but lost to Iowa, Minnesota and Indiana from late September to late October.

Their offense has been dismal all season, culminating in an awful 15-6 loss to Michigan State last on November 7. Instead of progressing in his second year as a starter, Bryce Underwood has ranged from disappointing to unacceptably bad. To the point where Whittingham benched him for backup Tommy Carr. All this has led to speculation and outright discussion around Michigan that boosters are preparing to pull together enough to buy Whittingham out after just one season. It also might explain why the normally uncontroversial coach is making headlines.

MICHIGAN HIRED KYLE WHITTINGHAM TO FIX ITS MESS. INSTEAD, HE’S CREATED AN EVEN BIGGER ONE WITH WOLVERINES

At a news conference ahead of this weekend's game, Whittingham praised Oregon head coach Dan Lanning, then took a shot at the Ducks' immense financial resources.

"Outstanding football coach, defensive-minded coach. That’s his background. Tireless recruiter. He really does a great job recruiting, and it doesn’t hurt that you have $50+ million dollars at your disposal to, in essence outbid everybody," he said. "Not everybody, but a lot of people. But that’s not his fault. That’s a credit. I mean, that’s a credit to their program and their dedication and desire to win and the support they have. NIL is the name of the game in recruiting these days. It’s shifted so much.

"It used to be the facilities you had and the tradition and all these other things, and now it’s, ‘Oh, this is all great, but these guys have a hundred grand more for me. So that’s a little bit of a factor to say the least. But not to take anything away from Dan, because he is an outstanding recruiter."

Maybe there's some personal animus there, stemming from a fight between the two over a recruit or recruits? Regardless of the motivations though, Whittingham's right that the Ducks have significant advantages over other teams. Lanning though, unsurprisingly heard about it and, well, didn't love it.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

On Wednesday, Lanning said he had "nothing to say," then said something back.

"I’ve got nothing to say to Coach Whit other than I think he’s an unbelievable coach, and I get it," he said. "They’re spending more of their money right now on their coaches that they’re letting go, so maybe it makes it hard to sign players.

"But I know they’ve signed a couple of guys that we weren’t able to compete with what they decided to do, and maybe a lot of that money is tied up for them in another player. I don’t know. But Coach Whittingham is an unbelievable coach. He’s a Hall of Fame coach. I’ve got nothing but respect for him."

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

That is definitely more than "nothing" to say!

Both coaches are right about their fronthanded criticisms and backhanded compliments. Lanning deserves a ton of credit for helping keep Oregon's season (mostly) on the rails, recovering after losses to UCLA and Illinois to beat Northwestern and then Ohio State in Columbus. But the Ducks entered 2026 with championship aspirations in large part because of their very expensive roster.

Yes, Dante Moore got hurt against USC, but that came after Oregon was thoroughly dismantled by Oklahoma State. And the money they have allowed them to sign Dylan Raiola, who started at Nebraska in 2025, as a backup. A luxury few other teams enjoy. They can outbid almost anyone if they really want to, or if they value a player more than the other team.

SIGN UP FOR THE DAILY OUTKICK NEWSLETTER

So Whittingham is right that Lanning is a great recruiter, a very good head coach, and also has immense resources at his disposal.

Lanning is right to take a pot shot at Michigan's coaching staff problems, including the $10 million buyout owed to Jason Beck after just a few months of a three-year deal. And he's also right that Whittingham has been a great head coach his entire career. Just an incredible exchange of mutual praise, admiration, and sarcastic criticisms.

Before the season, Oregon-Michigan seemed like one of the big games on the calendar, must-see TV for college football fans. Most of the shine is off, now that the Wolverines are buried and Oregon is clinging to hopes of reaching the Big Ten Conference Championship, but the war of words off the field has made the on-field game must-see TV all over again.

item.title: Brewers' Jacob Misiorowski, Yankees' Cam Schlittler named unanimous Cy Young Award winners for 2026 MLB season
item.description: Jacob Misiorowski was the first Cy Young Award and World Series winner in the same season since Randy Johnson, while Cam Schlittler's first full season resulted in the award.
item.content:encoded:
Milwaukee Brewers’ Jacob Misiorowski and New York Yankees’ Cam Schlittler were named unanimous Cy Young Award winners on Wednesday, confirming what many believed would be the case as the two most dominant starters in baseball during the 2026 MLB season.

Misiorowski, who led a Brewers pitching staff to the franchise’s first-ever World Series title, received all 30 first-place votes by the Baseball Writers’ Association of America. Philadelphia Phillies’ left-hander Cristopher Sanchez came in second place, while Atlanta Braves veteran lefty Chris Sale finished third.

Schlittler, in his first full season with the Yankees, was a breakout star in a loaded rotation. He also received all 30 first-place votes, while Toronto Blue Jays’ Dylan Cease and Cleveland Guardians Parker Messick finished second and third, respectively.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

It was also announced on Wednesday that San Diego Padres closer Mason Miller and Blue Jays closer Louis Varland won the inaugural Reliever of the Year award for their respective leagues.

Misiorowski, the 24-year-old with a lightning rod for an arm that lives in the triple digits with his fastball, had the best ERA for a starter in baseball this season at 1.80, while collecting 252 strikeouts in 30 starts, which also led the league.

As the Brewers went on to win 103 regular-season games, "The Miz" pitched to a 0.80 WHIP, while owning a 6.6 fWAR which led all pitchers.

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

Misiorowski became the fourth Brewers pitcher to ever win the Cy Young Award, the latest being Corbin Burnes in 2021. Pete Vuckovich (1982) and Rollie Fingers (1981) collected the award as well.

Even sweeter, Misiorowski was the first pitcher since Hall of Famer Randy Johnson to win both the Cy Young and a World Series in the same season, which he did as a member of the Arizona Diamondbacks in 2001.

At 6-foot-7, Misiorowski’s fastball against Pete Crow-Armstrong of the Chicago Cubs during a June game became the fastest pitch ever thrown by a starter in the Statcast era after clocking at 105.5 mph. He averaged 100.6 mph on his fastballs, throwing more than 1,000 pitches at that speed or faster during the season.

In the American League, though, Schlittler, standing at 6-foot-6, also delivered a triple-digit four-seamer. Misiorowski certainly has him beat for the best fastball, but in his first full season with the Yankees, he was as dominant as they believed he could be following an impressive showing in 2025.

But nobody in the Bronx expected the 25-year-old to be the ace of a rotation that featured Gerrit Cole, the Yankees’ most-recent Cy Young winner in 2023, Carlos Rodon, and Max Fried.

Schlittler owned an AL-best 1.95 ERA with 239 strikeouts across 33 starts. The Yankees had the best ERA as a pitching staff in the regular season, and Schlitter was a key reason why, giving up one run or fewer in 21 of those 33 outings.

And it wasn’t a home crowd that got him going extra when it was his turn to take the mound. It seemed Schlitter relished moments on the road, owning a 1.16 ERA over 17 starts away from Yankee Stadium.

Schlittler, a Massachusetts native who grew up a Boston Red Sox fan and is now universally hated by the fan base he loves to troll on social media, is a product of the Yankees’ minor league system. As a seventh-round draft choice out of Northeastern, Schlittler wasn’t always throwing gas with a devastating curveball mixed in with a cutter and sinker.

After mechanical changes, adding muscle and more, the Yankees saw Schlitter’s velocity rising from the low 90s to the upper 90s, with times where he’d top out at triple digits. Like Misiorowski, Schlitter has the ability to not only blow it past you, but place his heaters wherever he wishes, making it that much harder to get on base.

Schlittler proved he wasn’t just a one-hit wonder after his tremendous Game 3 of the AL Wild Card Series in 2025, where he held his childhood team scoreless for eight innings with 12 strikeouts. He dominated his way through the Yankees’ schedule and ultimately picked up another win against the Red Sox in the AL Wild Card Series this past season, where he pitched Game 1 as the team’s ace.

Both pitchers have bright careers ahead of them, with one already notching a World Series ring under his belt.

item.title: Titans' Calvin Ridley gives his side of Nashville airport 'incident' with valet, awaits possible charges
item.description: Calvin Ridley said he took his keys from a Nashville airport valet's hand during a late-night dispute over a missing ticket, and the valet claimed a broken finger.
item.content:encoded:
Calvin Ridley, the veteran Tennessee Titans wide receiver, gave his side of an "incident" that occurred at Nashville International Airport this past weekend.

Ridley acknowledged his involvement in the incident confirmed by the Titans, describing it as a back-and-forth argument with an airport valet while trying to retrieve the keys to his truck.

Speaking with reporters, Ridley said he took his keys from the valet’s hands when he didn’t have the ticket needed to retrieve them, though he said he showed other documents proving the truck was his.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

"I took my keys out of his hand," Ridley said, via Yahoo Sports. "I didn't have the ticket. Once you don't have the ticket, you show him your ID, you fill out a form. I also showed him a picture, I also showed him more that it's my truck.

"My wife and kids was at the top. My mom was at the top. I came down by myself to get it. It's 11 p.m. at night. They gave me the hardest time to get my truck. I just got my keys, got the registration.

"They wanted the registration. I gave them the registration after I got the keys. My wife came down. We got in the truck and left."

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

Ridley added the valet suffered an injury to one of his fingers. He was asked about the nature of the injury, but Ridley said, "I don’t know what I did. I didn’t look at nothing."

"He yelled I broke his finger," Ridley said. "I don’t know what happened."

Titans head coach Robert Saleh categorized the incident as "a very minor miscommunication."

Ridley said he has yet to hear from law enforcement, but a report from A to Z Sports on Monday stated the valet wants to press charges. It remains unclear as of Wednesday if charges have been filed.

The report also cited sources that said Ridley was frustrated when the valet wouldn’t give him his keys. Ridley also confirmed the report stating he didn’t have his ticket and the valet couldn’t verify his truck.

The reason for the reporter asking Ridley on Wednesday if the valet’s finger was cut was due to the report stating "one of the keys (or something on the keychain) cut the valet’s hand in the process" of him trying to take his keys.

Ridley was expected to be a potential NFL trade candidate, as the Titans sit at 1-7 entering Week 10 in yet another struggling season.

In Saleh’s first season, which includes offensive coordinator Brian Daboll’s first year working with quarterback Cam Ward and the rest of the roster, the 31-year-old hasn’t had a productive year. He has just six catches for 91 yards in seven games, which led to the trade deadline rumors.

Ridley is in his third season with the Titans and his eighth year in the NFL.

item.title: Blue states elect Democrats who supported permanent cash handout policy as part of mayors coalition
item.description: Five former Mayors for a Guaranteed Income coalition members won higher office, raising questions about direct cash assistance becoming permanent policy.
item.content:encoded:
Proponents of guaranteed income programs are declaring victory following the midterm elections after several key allies won statewide and federal offices across the country.

Five former members of the Mayors for a Guaranteed Income (MGI) coalition — along with officials from partner organizations — won election to higher office, while voters approved multiple direct-cash ballot measures nationwide.

The most prominent victory came in Georgia, where MGI founding member and former Atlanta Mayor Keisha Lance Bottoms was elected governor, becoming the first Black woman elected to lead the state.

GEORGIA GOVERNOR'S MANSION PROJECTED TO FLIP BLUE FOR FIRST TIME IN NEARLY 30 YEARS

"Support for guaranteed income has been steadily growing since we launched the first pilot in 2019," MGI President Michael D. Tubbs told Fox News Digital.

MGI noted that more than 60 bills involving cash-based policies similar to guaranteed income have been introduced across 15 states.

Tubbs, who served as mayor of Stockton, California, from 2017 to 2021, also founded Counties for a Guaranteed Income (CGI) and Legislators for a Guaranteed Income.

"Previous polling showed a majority of voters support direct, unconditional cash assistance, and now we've seen several champions who led guaranteed income programs at the local level ascend to higher office in the most recent elections," Tubbs said. 

"I hope the newly elected Democratic House and Senate will continue to prioritize affordability and make guaranteed income a permanent policy for Americans."

MAYORS WANT TO KEEP HANDING OUT FREE CASH AFTER FEDERAL FUNDS DRIED UP

Two current MGI members secured seats in the U.S. House of Representatives:

Neither Biss nor Cognetti responded to Fox News Digital’s request for comment.

Meanwhile, Counties for a Guaranteed Income (CGI) — MGI's sister network — saw two of its prominent members elected to higher office:

None of the other newly elected officials responded to Fox News Digital's requests for comment.

Cook County, Illinois, previously made headlines for establishing what officials described as the nation's first permanent guaranteed income program at the county level. To sustain the program after federal funding from the American Rescue Plan Act (ARPA) expired, the Cook County Board of Commissioners approved $7.5 million for guaranteed income as part of its fiscal year 2026 budget.

Tubbs previously told Fox News Digital the federal government should follow Cook County's lead by establishing a federal direct-cash assistance program.

"We have wars in Iran, regime change in Venezuela. We get it, the healthcare system and the big, ugly bill," Tubbs said in March. "So, people are saying that social safety is being frayed.

"That wealth is further being taken from the many and given to the few, and there has to be a government solution because this is a government-caused problem. … Inflation, unaffordability, this is all a direct result of government policy," Tubbs added.

According to MGI, guaranteed basic income initiatives have expanded across the country, with more than 100 pilot programs launched since 2018. MGI has grown into a coalition of more than 150 mayors, promoting pilots that offer eligible participants payments of as much as $1,000 per month with no spending restrictions.

However, with federal pandemic relief dollars drying up, questions remain about whether local governments can afford to make these programs permanent through local taxes.

AS AMERICANS ARE CRUSHED BY AFFORDABILITY, GROWING TREND OF MAYORS PUSHING CASH HANDOUTS AS THE ANSWER

Other progressive advocacy groups are pushing for permanent taxpayer-funded guaranteed income programs at both state and federal levels.

The Economic Security Project (ESP), founded in 2016 by a network of entrepreneurs, activists and philanthropists, has backed over 100 guaranteed income pilots nationwide.

ESP Director of Cash Initiatives Shafeka Hashash directed Fox News Digital to a post highlighting election results that favored guaranteed income advocates.

"Michigan. Dr. Abdul El-Sayed is a longtime cash champion. He spoke at the 2024 GI [Guaranteed Income] Now conference and contributed to our 2025 report ‘The Resilience Factor: Cash as a Tool Toward Better Health for Young Families.’ In one of the toughest Senate races in the country, his campaign centered on a single tagline: 'Money out of politics. Money in your pocket,'" Hashash wrote.

FORMER CALIFORNIA MAYOR PUSHES GUARANTEED INCOME AS FIX FOR AFFORDABILITY CRISIS

El-Sayed, who won Michigan's U.S. Senate election, has supported direct-cash programs aimed at reducing poverty. While his campaign platform centered on universal healthcare through Medicare-for-all, raising the federal minimum wage and strengthening safety net programs, cash advocates view his election as a key policy win.

Hashash also highlighted veteran allies returning to Capitol Hill: "Ohio. Sherrod Brown, a longtime champion of the Child Tax Credit, returns to the Senate with new allies. Eight of the 10 new Democratic senators are on the record supporting the CTC and included it in their platforms."

item.title: Suspected DUI driver arrested on 3 murder counts after deadly North Hollywood crash, police say
item.description: A suspected 61-year-old DUI driver was arrested on three murder counts after a North Hollywood crash killed three women and injured two others.
item.content:encoded:
A 61-year-old man suspected of driving under the influence was arrested on three counts of murder after his minivan crashed into pedestrians and a food vendor near a North Hollywood Metro station, killing three women and critically injuring two others, Los Angeles police announced Wednesday.

The Los Angeles Police Department identified the driver as Ihor Demianenko of Valley Village, who investigators determined was under the influence after Tuesday evening's deadly crash. 

He was arrested on three counts of murder, and his bail was set at $6.03 million, police said.

The crash happened around 5:55 p.m. Tuesday when Demianenko was driving a white Toyota Sienna southbound on Lankershim Boulevard, just south of Chandler Boulevard, according to an LAPD news release.

MARIJUANA USERS MAY FACE HIDDEN DRIVING DANGER THAT STANDARD TESTS CAN MISS

Police said the minivan veered right at an unsafe speed, struck a food vendor and pedestrians near the sidewalk and continued moving before becoming stuck inside a building.

Los Angeles Fire Department paramedics pronounced three women dead at the crash site. Police said the victims were Hispanic women between 40 and 60 years old whose identities have not been released pending notification of their families.

Two other women, both Hispanic and between 50 and 55 years old, were taken to a hospital in critical condition.

CALIFORNIA MOM HAS BOTH LEGS AMPUTATED AFTER SUSPECTED IMPAIRED DRIVER PLOWS INTO HER RESTAURANT LUNCH TABLE

Demianenko suffered minor injuries and was taken to a hospital for treatment before his arrest, police said.

Los Angeles Mayor Karen Bass expressed condolences to the victims' families following the crash.

"I'm heartbroken for the families of everyone impacted," Bass said in a statement posted on X. "We will continue to provide updates as more information becomes available."

CHARTER BUS DRIVER WHO ALLEGEDLY CAUSED CRASH KILLING 5 IN VIRGINIA CHARGED WITH INVOLUNTARY MANSLAUGHTER

LAPD Chief Jim McDonnell previously said investigators would conduct a thorough investigation into the circumstances surrounding the collision.

"It'll be a prolonged but a very deliberate investigation to determine what happened here," McDonnell told reporters. "Our hearts go out to the families of the victims that were struck here tonight."

The LAPD's Valley Traffic Division is investigating the collision. Anyone with information is asked to contact investigators at 818-644-8114 or 818-644-8117.

Fox News Digital's Landon Mion contributed to this report.

item.title: Twice-deported United cockpit suspect granted asylum after transgender persecution claim: DHS
item.description: DHS says a twice-deported Honduran national won asylum claiming transgender persecution before allegedly trying to storm a United Airlines cockpit.
item.content:encoded:
A twice-deported Honduran national accused of trying to storm the cockpit of a United Airlines flight after allegedly claiming to have a bomb was granted asylum after telling immigration authorities he feared being killed in his home country because he was transgender, the Department of Homeland Security DHS confirmed to Fox News.

Rony Alexander Gomez-Alberto, 34, was granted asylum by an immigration judge after his third attempted illegal entry into the United States in 2019, according to DHS, which accused him of exploiting weaknesses in the asylum system.

In an excerpt of his asylum application provided by DHS, Gomez-Alberto checked "Yes" when asked whether he feared harm or mistreatment if returned to his home country.

TRUMP PUTS ASYLUM LAWYERS ‘ON NOTICE’ WITH NEW FRONT IN WAR ON FRAUD

"I am also afraid that I will be killed — either by private citizens or the police — in both of these countries because I am transgender," he allegedly wrote, according to the application.

"This criminal illegal alien attempted to storm the cockpit, hijack a plane and claimed he had a bomb. Thanks to law enforcement, he is now behind bars," DHS Secretary Markwayne Mullin said in a statement. 

"This twice-deported criminal illegal alien was allowed into our country because of a weak asylum system that allowed him to game the system."

Gomez-Alberto was arrested after United Airlines Flight 2174 landed in New Orleans Nov. 9 after the alleged attempt at a cockpit breach.

MAN ACCUSED OF THREATENING TO HIJACK UNITED FLIGHT SAYS IT WAS A DRUNKEN JOKE

He is being held without bond on charges of terrorizing, communicating false information of planned arson and being a fugitive from justice, according to Fox News Digital's earlier reporting.

Newly obtained emergency radio audio, reported by Fox News Digital, captured authorities' response.

"We have him at the back door. The back door has been breached by him," someone can be heard in the radio call saying.

DHS previously confirmed that Gomez-Alberto was apprehended by Border Patrol after illegally entering the United States near El Indio, Texas, in September 2011 and Columbus, New Mexico, in October 2014. He was deported from the United States following both encounters.

EXCLUSIVE: WOMAN ALLEGEDLY RAPED BY ILLEGAL ALIEN AFTER CLINTON-APPOINTED FEDERAL JUDGE ORDERED HIS RELEASE

Border Patrol arrested him again in 2019 after an attempted illegal entry near San Ysidro, California.

ICE released Gomez-Alberto from custody in January 2020 following an immigration judge's order, pending removal proceedings, DHS previously said. The agency now says an immigration judge subsequently granted him asylum.

ICE lodged a detainer with the Jefferson Parish Sheriff's Office on Nov. 10, requesting notification before his release from custody.

The Department of Justice and Jefferson Parish Sheriff's Office did not immediately respond to Fox News Digital's requests for comment.

Fox News Digital's Kelsie Cairns contributed to this reporting.

item.title: Rams star Puka Nacua out for an 'extended period' after suffering injury on final play of win
item.description: Puka Nacua sprained his MCL and PCL and sustained turf toe, and Los Angeles Rams head coach Sean McVay said he will be out for an extended period of time.
item.content:encoded:
The Los Angeles Rams will be without their top wide receiver for an extended period.

Puka Nacua sprained his MCL and PCL and sustained a turf toe injury during the Rams' 20-13 win over the Washington Commanders on Sunday. He will be sidelined for an extended period, coach Sean McVay said Wednesday.

"We won’t place him on IR due to some semantics with the roster and things like that, but he’ll be out for an extended period of time," McVay said, according to The Athletic.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

Although Nacua missed two games earlier this season due to injury, he has been incredibly productive when healthy. In seven games, the two-time Pro Bowler has 70 catches for 715 yards and four touchdowns.

Compounding the Rams' problems, they are now without their top two wide receivers, as Davante Adams remains sidelined with a hamstring injury he suffered in Week 6. The Rams play the Green Bay Packers in Week 12 on Thanksgiving Eve, and McVay said the team is currently targeting that crucial NFC matchup for Adams' return.

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

In six games this season, the six-time Pro Bowler has 30 catches for 480 yards and four touchdowns. Without Nacua and Adams, the Rams are incredibly thin at wide receiver. They hope Konata Mumpfield, Tutu Atwell, CJ Daniels and Xavier Smith can step up in their absence while also leaning on their deep group of tight ends.

Despite their precarious situation at wide receiver, McVay cited Adams' expected return as a reason the Rams didn't acquire a receiver at the trade deadline.

"It kind of takes two [to trade], and you’ve got to be able to see what you’re willing to give, what’s out there, what’s out there as far as envisioning things," McVay said, according to The Athletic. "I think with a lot of the moves that you guys will be wondering about, what we are optimistic about is Davante’s return is sooner [rather] than later."

The Rams have won their last three games to improve to 5-4 this season. The Arizona Cardinals (3-6) beat them earlier this season, and Los Angeles will look to avenge that loss when the teams meet again Sunday at 4:05 p.m. ET. The Cardinals will start rookie Carson Beck at quarterback.

item.title: Tunnel to Towers pays off mortgages for 30 military families in Veterans Day tribute: 'A great sacrifice'
item.description: Tunnel to Towers Foundation announced mortgage payoffs for 30 Gold Star families on Veterans Day, part of its goal to deliver 343 homes in 2026.
item.content:encoded:
The Tunnel to Towers Foundation marked Veterans Day Wednesday by announcing mortgage payoffs for 30 families of fallen military heroes across the country, helping ensure their loved ones have a permanent place to call home.

The families span 22 states and represent nearly every branch of the U.S. military, according to the foundation, which provides mortgage-free homes to surviving spouses and children of service members and first responders who died in the line of duty or from service-related illnesses.

Tunnel to Towers Foundation Chairman and CEO Frank Siller shared the news Wednesday on "Fox & Friends" to discuss the mortgages, its housing program for homeless veterans in Pennsylvania and its upcoming Season of Hope initiative for firefighters' families.

9/11 HERO’S MEMORY PRESERVED THROUGH MASSIVE EFFORT TO ‘DO GOOD’ FOR VETS, FIRST RESPONDERS: ‘HIS LEGACY’

"No. 1 is that we are paying off 30 mortgages to Gold Star families that lost their loved ones for our country. Many of them are dying of burn pit cancers, just like many of our first responders are still dying from 9/11 illnesses. It's very sad," Siller said. 

"So, on a day like today, we want to make sure that America doesn't forget that there's a great sacrifice always being made for our country. We get to live in this great country. There are people out there that are still dying for us."

The Veterans Day announcement is part of a larger commitment to deliver 343 mortgage-free homes in 2026, a tribute to the 343 New York City firefighters who lost their lives during the Sept. 11, 2001, terrorist attacks.

The milestone comes as the nation commemorates the 25th anniversary of 9/11, a tragedy that inspired the foundation's creation and its ongoing mission to support military families and first responders.

"So, we made a promise this year for the 25th anniversary that we're going to deliver 343 mortgage-free homes this year, one for every firefighter who died on 9/11. That's almost a house a day," Siller said. 

"From Thanksgiving to the Christmas is the remainder of those homes, over 60 homes that we'll be delivering, and it hit our 343 mark for the 25th anniversary."

Among those whose families were recognized Wednesday were Army Lt. Col. David Briseno of Grand Prairie, Texas; Marine Corps Master Sgt. Khanh Tuan "Shane" Nguyen of Annapolis, Maryland; Army Sgt. Brandon Minneman of Olympia, Washington; and Navy Chief Petty Officer Ernest Lopez Jr. of Oakdale, California.

Other recipients included families in New York, Georgia, Tennessee, Illinois, Massachusetts and several more states.

Through its Gold Star Family Home Program, the foundation seeks to ease the financial burden on families coping with the loss of a loved one who served the country.

AMERICA'S WOUNDED, STRUGGLING VETERANS GET BRAND-NEW HOMES BUILT BY FLORIDA TEENS

The program provides mortgage-free homes to eligible surviving spouses with young children, offering long-term housing stability following the death of a parent.

In addition to the mortgage payoffs, Tunnel to Towers celebrated the grand opening of its Harrisburg Veterans Village in Pennsylvania on Veterans Day, expanding its efforts to combat homelessness among former service members. The new development sits on the former Phoenix Mill property, where construction began in April 2025.

The foundation transformed the waterfront site on the Susquehanna River into a residential community featuring a 61-unit apartment complex and 20 one-bedroom comfort homes. The development is designed to house more than 80 veterans in need of permanent housing while providing access to services intended to help residents rebuild their lives.

Those services include job training, assistance obtaining veterans benefits, mental health support and addiction treatment.

STEEL ACROSS AMERICA ENDS ITS CROSS-COUNTRY 9/11 MEMORIAL AT NY GIANTS GAME

"I said, 'Hey, think about somebody who's overseas protecting us, right, and the guy next to him gets blown up, and it happens over and over again. They come back here to the states, and they're not all part of the military anymore. Now they have to assimilate back into society.’ A lot of them have real problems doing that, and they end up on the streets. It's not acceptable," Siller said.

"A couple of years ago, we, Tunnel for Towers, we made a promise we're going to eradicate homelessness amongst our veterans. In the last three years, we've taken 27,500 homeless veterans off the streets.

"We build these beautiful hotels, and then we remodel them into apartments for these permanent apartments for the older homeless veterans, and we put comfort homes on these properties. They're 500-square-foot houses, and they have their own homes."

The foundation said its approach goes beyond providing shelter by addressing the emotional, financial and medical challenges that can contribute to homelessness among veterans.

Tunnel to Towers launched its Homeless Veteran Program in 2022 with the goal of ensuring that veterans who served their country do not have to live on its streets.

Since the program began, the organization says it has provided housing assistance and supportive services to more than 20,000 veterans and 10,000 children.

The Harrisburg location joins Veterans Villages already operating in Memphis, Tennessee; North Charleston, South Carolina; Houston, Texas; and Atlanta, Georgia.

The foundation also supports affiliated veteran housing programs in Riverside and West Los Angeles, California, and Austin, Texas.

Another Veterans Village is scheduled to open Dec. 9 in Denver, Colorado, while seven additional developments are under construction and expected to open in 2027.

item.title: Bengals coach Zac Taylor acknowledges fault in failed trade for Eagles edge rusher Arnold Ebiketie
item.description: Zac Taylor revealed Duke Tobin's apology after a 2027 compensatory pick forfeiture derailed the Arnold Ebiketie trade with the Eagles at the deadline.
item.content:encoded:
Bengals coach Zac Taylor acknowledged Cincinnati deserved blame after its failed attempt to acquire Arnold Ebiketie from the Philadelphia Eagles before Tuesday’s trade deadline.

Taylor shared details Wednesday about how the process unfolded from the Bengals’ perspective, reading a prepared statement from Bengals director of football Duke Tobin. "Duke was very explicit with me when he came and spoke to me about how he wanted this portrayed," Taylor said as he began explaining why the roster move ultimately fell through. "I'm not comfortable doing it, but I'm going to do what he asked."

Tobin is the team's de facto general manager. He said the Bengals underestimated the cost of replacing Cashius Howell and emphasized that Philadelphia was a willing trade partner.

"We did make an effort to put some depth in there in place of Cashius [Howell]. As we got into it, obviously it was going to be a little more costly than we initially anticipated. He's really apologetic about it and wants to make clear [that] Philly was a great trade partner. It was on our end."

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

An initial report from NFL Network stated that the Bengals and Eagles decided on a deal that would send edge rusher Arnold Ebiketie to Cincinnati. The Bengals were set to give up a sixth-round pick in 2027, but the agreement apparently started going off the rails as the teams worked through the final details and tried to get the deal over the finish line.

MAXX CROSBY SAYS EVERYTHING HAPPENS FOR A REASON AFTER TRADE TO THE RAVENS FALLS THROUGH

ESPN reported Wednesday, citing sources, that it became clear to the Bengals that the team would need to give up a compensatory draft pick to finalize the trade. The additional compensation prompted Cincinnati back out of the proposed deal.

CHRISTIAN MCCAFFREY RECALLS 'WHIRLWIND' ORDEAL OF SHOCKING TRADE THAT SENT HIM FROM PANTHERS TO 49ERS

Questions remain about when and how the Bengals realized they would have to surrender the compensatory pick to complete the trade. The pick was awarded after Cincinnati lost more qualifying free agents than it signed, includingTrey Hendrickson.

Nick Korte posted on X about the potential loss of the pick after the trade was first reported as agreed to but before news emerged that the deal had fallen through.

Korte’s X profile identifies him as affiliated with OverTheCap, and he regularly shares NFL salary-cap news on the platform.

Taylor said he did not ask Tobin for details Tuesday because they did not matter to him.

"I didn't even ask the question," Taylor noted. "It doesn't really matter to me. It probably took three minutes of my day yesterday away from watching tape. Got a lot of faith in how [the front office] operates and we'll just move forward with it."

The Bengals defeated the Atlanta Falcons in the NFL’s first game in Madrid on Sunday to earn their fourth consecutive victory. Cincinnati hosts AFC North rival Pittsburgh Steelers in Week 10.

item.title: El-Sayed tells Hegseth to resign after impeachment effort fails: 'Make it easy for everybody'
item.description: Abdul El-Sayed told Secretary of War Pete Hegseth directly to resign on CNN, calling him "really bad" at his job and saying he has mishandled the war in Iran.
item.content:encoded:
Sen.-elect Abdul El-Sayed, D-Mich., called on Secretary of War Pete Hegseth to resign Tuesday, asking him, "Why are you still doing this job?"

Speaking with CNN's Kaitlan Collins, El-Sayed was asked whether Democrats should revive the failed impeachment attempt against Hegseth.

"Can you imagine being Pete Hegseth right now? Like, why are you still in your job? I mean it's an open question, like, 'Pete, like really, just open question, why are you still doing this job? You are really bad at this. You are failing your responsibility, you have mishandled this war and nobody really actually understands what it is you're about,'" El-Sayed said.

He spoke directly to the camera and said Hegseth was fighting a new culture war every day, but that he was supposed to be "waging an actual war that is actually illegal on its own terms."

DEMOCRATS RALLY BEHIND GOP LAWMAKER'S HEGSETH IMPEACHMENT PUSH, SIGNAL MORE TO COME IN JANUARY

"So, just resign. Make it easy for everybody instead of, in the end, getting taken out because that is clearly what's happening. So, Pete, just take it from me. Like, you're not good at this," El-Sayed added.

House Republicans killed an impeachment effort led by Rep. Thomas Massie, R-Ky., on Tuesday, by voting 211-204 to refer the resolution to the House Judiciary Committee and avoid a full vote on impeachment. 

All Democrats who voted opposed the motion, but 11 Democrats were absent.

President Donald Trump celebrated the failed impeachment effort in a Truth Social post, calling Massie a "total loser" and praising Hegseth's record on recruitment and military operations in Venezuela and Iran.

Collins asked El-Sayed during the CNN interview, "I mean you're talking directly to Pete Hegseth. What do you say to those 11 Democrats who didn't show up to vote tonight?"

HEGSETH IMPEACHMENT VOTE LOOMS AS HOUSE REPUBLICANS PRIVATELY WARN IT COULD PASS

El-Sayed told Democrats to show up and "do your job," and Collins said it was "surprising" that Democratic absences helped prevent a vote on the impeachment articles.

The Michigan senator-elect said he fielded questions from voters while on the campaign trail about high gas and grocery prices and attributed those costs to the war in Iran.

"Pete Hegseth has aided and abetted a president who we all know is way out of his league," he said. "And, so, you know, I think it is important for us to be recognizing that Pete Hegseth himself is the tie to the affordability that all of us crave when it comes to this administration.

"So, look, you know, obviously I'm not going to be in a position to vote to impeach, and I will assess any impeachment that is done on its own merits, but it's really quite clear that Pete Hegseth is failing his responsibilities as secretary of defense."

The White House and the Department of War did not immediately return Fox News Digital's request for comment. 

THE OVERLOOKED WAY THE IRAN WAR IS MAKING GROCERIES, AMAZON PACKAGES AND NEW HOMES MORE EXPENSIVE

Hegseth remained defiant during a news conference Tuesday, pushing back against the impeachment effort. 

He said he stood behind military operations in Iran, Venezuela and Yemen, describing them as lawful.

"What one disgruntled and defeated congressman is attempting is not oversight. It's not accountability. It's a political spectacle, a personal manifesto driven by ego and resentment," Hegseth said. 

"Time for one man's final days in Congress to try to do damage to this president, this country and, most irresponsibly, the warriors who defend it."

Y. David Scharf, a government strategies and controversies attorney, told Fox News Digital in a statement, "Democrats could spend the next two years trying to impeach Pete Hegseth and end up making him stronger.

"Congress may have every right to investigate, demand documents and subpoena witnesses," he continued. "But there’s a world of difference between holding an administration accountable and trying to remove someone simply because you don’t like his policies.

"Calling for Hegseth’s resignation is easy," Scharf added. "Actually removing him requires a two-thirds vote in the Senate. And if Democrats can’t even get their own members to show up for a vote, how do they expect to convince Republicans to join them?"

item.title: Former Giants coach defends star player Malik Nabers against character questions from broadcast analyst
item.description: Wink Martindale says someone may have put criticism in Greg Olsen's ear about Malik Nabers, suggesting motives tied to the Giants star's contract.
item.content:encoded:
When his character came into question, Giants star wideout Malik Nabers took to social media to take on former player and TV analyst Greg Olsen, who criticized the receiver’s sideline demeanor during Sunday's broadcast.

One former New York Giants coach is running to Nabers' defense. Ex-Giants defensive coordinator Wink Martindale, who had a messy split with the team in 2024, harbors no bad blood toward the receiver and spoke up to defend Nabers against Olsen's critique.

"I'm with Malik on this. Somebody put that in his ear, whether it's to keep his contract down for the next year when they want to extend him or whatever it is, I don't know. But just keep playing," Martindale said, appearing on Giants insider Pat Leonard's "Talkin' Ball" podcast.

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

"I love the kid. I love his competitiveness."

During the Giants' visit to Philadelphia on Sunday, Olsen and boothmate Joe Davis kept pointing to Nabers' "negative" body language on the sideline. They also called him out for pouting after a Giants drive finished with an Isaiah Likely touchdown.

"His body language has been terrible today," Davis said.

KANSAS CITY CHIEFS STAR DEFENSIVE LINEMAN CHRIS JONES CAUGHT IN SCREAMING MATCH WITH COACHES ON SIDELINES

Olsen proved more frustrated with Nabers.

"I have played with a lot of really good wide receivers, a lot [of] really good players. There's never been a great wide receiver who hasn't demanded the ball. That kind of comes with the territory. But there is a very fine line between being demanding, being a competitor, and all those great things. That's great. It just can never cross that it feels like it takes away from the success of your teammates.

MALIK NABERS REVEALS HOW GIANTS COACH JOHN HARBAUGH HELPED HIM OVERCOME HIS ACL INJURY FEARS

"So when your teammate catches a wide-open touchdown, you need to be the happiest guy on the field. You can't still be worried about your targets. That's the fine line. He is a talented, young, really good player. You've just got to keep it in check."

Martindale added, "Think about all the great players that John Harbaugh's coached. Does he get blown up more because it's in New York? Of course it does. But it's nothing new for John."

Martindale knows a thing or two about friction inside New York's building. Following months of simmering tension during the 2023 season, his Giants tenure imploded in January 2024 after head coach Brian Daboll fired Martindale’s trusted defensive assistants. Martindale reportedly cursed out Daboll, stormed out, and mutually parted ways.

Despite showing visible frustration during the Giants' 19-11 win in Philadelphia, where he had five catches for 43 yards after four straight 100-yard games, Nabers' commitment was never questioned by his locker room.

Giants players publicly defended him as a "good teammate, " with running back Cam Skattebo noting that Nabers' sideline annoyance when lacking targets simply reflects a competitive edge teammates "love to see."

item.title: El Salvador-backed air assault destroys Haiti gang headquarters amid search for missing troops
item.description: Helicopters struck Haiti gang compound, dozens fled and President Bukele touted the assault amid a search for four missing Salvadoran personnel.
item.content:encoded:
El Salvador's president on Tuesday said the country's military helped deliver a devastating air assault against the headquarters of one of Haiti's most powerful criminal gangs, which has been linked to mass kidnappings, weapons trafficking and extortion.

Airstrikes targeted strongholds belonging to 400 Mawozo and the home of its leader, Lanmò San Jou, Salvadoran President Nayib Bukele said.

The attack took place Sunday near Port-au-Prince and was carried out by a Haitian police task force backed by Salvadoran troops, The Miami Herald reported.

BUKELE WARNS HAITIAN GANG LEADERS THAT HIS FORCES WILL 'FINISH' THEM AS HE DID IN EL SALVADOR

The operation appears to be part of an ongoing military effort in response to the disappearance of four Salvadoran members of a U.N.-backed security mission abducted in a gang ambush near Port-au-Prince Oct. 18.

"We kept our promise," Bukele said in a post on X.

Videos showed several helicopters launching airstrikes against multiple compounds inside sprawling complexes. Dozens of people were also seen fleeing the properties on foot and motorbikes after the strikes.

"Most of them ran away without even trying to fight. What cowards!" Bukele said.

As many as 20 people are believed to have been killed in the operation, according to The Miami Herald, citing anonymous sources.

SUSPECTS IN HAITIAN PRESIDENT'S ASSASSINATION TRANSFERRED TO MIAMI, ACCUSED OF FUNDING PLOT WITH COVID FRAUD

Haitian Prime Minister Alix Didier Fils-Aimé on Tuesday thanked Bukele for his commitment to tackling the country's long-running gang crisis and restoring state control, while praising the efforts of the U.N.-backed Gang Suppression Force (GSF), the Haitian National Police, the Haitian Armed Forces and their international partners.

"I salute the commitment of the Salvadoran forces in the fight against gangs," he said.

"Hats off to President Nayib Bukele @nayibbukele for your support and commitment to the national fight against gangs. Haiti, El Salvador, GSF: same fight, same determination! The collaboration will continue. THE GANGS WILL GET NO SLEEP!"

After an Oct. 18 ambush, authorities recovered a burned armored vehicle with no trace of the four missing Salvadoran personnel, prompting El Salvador to deploy thousands of additional troops to assist in the search.

While Salvadoran officials believe the men were abducted and survived, one gang leader claimed they were dead.

The disappearance has become a national priority for Bukele, who has warned Haitian gang leaders that El Salvador is prepared to use overwhelming force if the men are not returned alive.

item.title: Illegal immigrant arrested after dragging, striking ICE officer in Chicago suburb: DHS
item.description: Jose Garnica-Naranjo, a Mexican citizen, allegedly dragged an ICE officer through a car window during a traffic stop in Chicago Heights, DHS said.
item.content:encoded:
FIRST ON FOX: An illegal immigrant with a prior criminal history was arrested Wednesday after allegedly dragging a U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) officer with his car while fleeing an arrest attempt outside Chicago, federal officials said.

Jose Garnica-Naranjo, 32, a Mexican citizen, was taken into custody a day after violently resisting a targeted immigration enforcement operation, according to the Department of Homeland Security.

"This illegal alien used his vehicle to assault one of our ICE officers, hospitalizing the officer," Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin said.

"Thankfully, the officer has since been released from the hospital. This is just the latest example of the staggering rise in anti-ICE violence, with our officers facing a more than 1,600% increase in assaults against them."

VENEZUELAN NATIONAL SHOT BY ICE OFFICER IN AUSTIN CHARGED WITH ASSAULTING FEDERAL OFFICER

ICE officers spotted Garnica-Naranjo leaving a home in Chicago Heights on Tuesday morning. Officers followed his car at a distance before attempting to initiate a traffic stop, DHS said.

When officers approached the vehicle, they instructed Garnica-Naranjo to turn off the engine, but he allegedly refused to comply.

"When officers attempted to remove him from the vehicle, Garnica accelerated and fled while an ERO Chicago officer was partially inside the vehicle through the driver-side window," DHS said in a statement.

ICE SAYS OFFICER SHOT AND KILLED ILLEGAL IMMIGRANT WHO TRIED TO RAM HIM WITH CAR IN HOUSTON

Garnica-Naranjo then drove over a raised center median planted with trees, causing the officer to be thrown from the vehicle, according to authorities.

As Garnica-Naranjo fled, his car struck the injured officer, who was subsequently taken to a local hospital. The officer suffered contusions, cuts and scrapes to his legs, though tests confirmed no broken bones.

ICE noted that Garnica-Naranjo's criminal record includes prior convictions for domestic violence and assault.

Mullin blamed violence against immigration officers on rhetoric from Democratic elected officials who have accused ICE of terrorizing neighborhoods during law enforcement operations.

"This is the result of anti-ICE rhetoric from sanctuary politicians like Illinois Governor J.B. Pritzker," he said. "DHS is calling on Governor Pritzker and all other sanctuary politicians to knock off this violent rhetoric and start cooperating with ICE before any more officers are injured in the line of duty."

item.title: Jamie Foxx’s daughter’s 18th birthday bash erupts in violence as deputies make arrests
item.description: Video footage shows violent fights erupting at SKVLK Fest, the annual Halloween music festival held at Jamie Foxx's California mansion. It doubled as his daughter's birthday party.
item.content:encoded:
A birthday celebration for Jamie Foxx's daughter descended into chaos when violent fights erupted Nov. 7.

The violence unfolded during SKVLK Fest, an annual Halloween music festival held at Foxx's California mansion. The party was reportedly coordinated by his daughter, Anelise, who turned 18 Oct. 3. 

Originally scheduled for Halloween, the event was postponed because of rain.

Video obtained by TMZ from the music festival-turned-birthday bash shows a fight that broke out among guests. Several people were seen punching each other and rolling around on the ground.

JAMIE FOXX THINKS 'GOD SOMETIMES SLIPS AWAY' IN HOLLYWOOD

The Ventura County Sheriff's Department later confirmed multiple physical altercations took place during the party.

"It was reported to Sheriff’s Communications that a male juvenile suspect allegedly slashed another male juvenile with a knife, causing a response from patrol deputies," a statement shared by authorities read. 

"Once on scene, deputies and investigators were told a juvenile victim suffered a superficial laceration to the victim’s neck believed to be from a knife."

After investigating, the Ventura County Sheriff's Department determined the victim was not assaulted with a knife and that his injury appeared to have resulted from a physical altercation.

Authorities said an estimated 3,000 or more people attended the event.

The following day, a third victim reported he was assaulted near the concert stage after being knocked to the ground in a mosh pit, according to the police statement. He said he was repeatedly punched and kicked before losing consciousness. He also reported his phone and money had been stolen. His phone was later recovered and returned.

The Ventura County Sheriff's Department is seeking video from the party as the investigations continue. So far, two juvenile suspects have been arrested.

It's unclear whether Foxx was at the party. The actor has been filming in Australia, according to his latest Instagram posts.

Fox News Digital reached out to Foxx's representative for more information.

SKVLK Fest is an annual Halloween-themed music and carnival festival reportedly organized by Anelise. What began as a family celebration has grown into a large entertainment event featuring celebrity performances, carnival rides, costumes and social media personalities.

The festival has attracted major hip-hop and R&B performers. Its 2026 lineup included Offset, OhGeesy, 310babii and SuperDuperKyle. Previous performers have included GloRilla, Tyga, Ty Dolla $ign, Sexyy Red and YK Osiris.

item.title: Jeffries leaves door open to investigating major Trump ally as Democrats prepare to take power
item.description: Hakeem Jeffries says Democrats will "follow the facts" as Jamie Raskin and Robert Garcia prepare to lead oversight of Elon Musk and DOGE.
item.content:encoded:
House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries left the door open to a congressional investigation into Elon Musk as threats to probe both the Department of Government Efficiency (DOGE) and other Trump allies continue to heat up under a new Democratic House majority.

"We're going to follow the facts," Jeffries said about the potential investigation. "We're going to apply the law. We're gonna be guided by the Constitution."

Musk has emerged as a potential target of Democratic oversight, with some lawmakers calling for scrutiny of his time as head of the DOGE. 

The calls for an investigation come as Democrats have started rallying the party to look into alleged corruption under the Trump administration after coming out victorious in midterms.

SCHUMER, JEFFRIES SIDESTEP QUESTIONS ON NUKING FILIBUSTER, LAUNCHING ELON MUSK PROBE AFTER BLUE WAVE

Asked whether Musk should be investigated by the new Democratic majority, Jeffries declined to commit to a probe, instead pointing to the lawmakers expected to lead the party's oversight efforts.

"Jamie Raskin and Robert Garcia are going to lead our oversight efforts," Jeffries told Fox News Digital. "And I defer to them at the moment."

Raskin, D-Md., has already signaled that DOGE could face congressional scrutiny, telling Fox News Digital last week he believes an investigation is warranted, even as he acknowledged having no specific plan.

‘LAWYER UP’: DEMS IMMEDIATELY PUT TRUMP ON NOTICE AMID REPUBLICANS' MIDTERM BLOODBATH

"I had no specific plan," Raskin told Fox News Digital about the potential investigations. "Look … DOGE was a catastrophe for America, and at least one committee, I feel pretty certain, will investigate it. It needs to investigate it."

After taking the majority, the prospects for new investigations come with Raskin and Garcia positioned to be chairs of the House Judiciary and Oversight Committees.

Raskin, Garcia, Jeffries and Assistant Democratic Leader Joe Neguse have already begun strategizing plans for the investigative agenda.

Jeffries is in the running for speaker of the House after formally announcing his bid just a day after Democrats took back the majority in the midterm elections. Democrats have not been united in their decision to back Jeffries or another candidate to represent the party as House speaker.

REPORTER’S NOTEBOOK: HOUSE LEADERSHIP UP FOR GRABS AS GOP RECKONS WITH DEVASTATING LOSSES

Leadership elections for House Democrats will be held Nov. 18 and members will vote with "secret ballots" to keep their individual nominations private.

Jeffries will need a simple majority of Democrats to be nominated, but to be formally elected as House speaker, he’ll need to get 218 floor votes.

item.title: Nature and civilization collide once again as lost black bear sprints across South Florida street
item.description: Video captures a Florida black bear darting across a busy Naples road near I-75 as South Florida Everglades development pushes wildlife out.
item.content:encoded:
It's been quite a wild last few weeks for the citizens of suburban South Florida... literally!

Last week, I wrote about the floods all along the Atlantic coast of the Sunshine State contributing to a shark (or tarpon) sighting on the wet and wild streets of Fort Pierce.

Now, on the west coast of Florida, a video has emerged of an animal challenging motorists that feels more at home on an inland road than a scaly sea monster.

Folks in the Gulf coast city of Naples, FL, got quite a show this weekend when a black bear, seemingly lost on his way back to the woods, darted across a busy access road that runs adjacent to Interstate 75.

The footage shows a clearly confused black bear running around a busy street in a fairly densely populated area.

WATCH: YOUNG BEAR TAKES ROUGH TUMBLE FROM DENVER TREE AFTER WILDLIFE OFFICERS TRANQUILIZE IT

Naples has a reputation as a retirement town, but the metropolitan area that it sits in is home to about 400,000 people, so this isn't exactly a backwater part of the country where the citizens and wildlife coexist as one.

Another thing I can tell you having been to the area several times is that large sections of I-75 butt right up against the Florida Everglades, so there is a good chance this poor little guy wandered a little too far from home and ended up playing real-life "Frogger."

BLACK BEARS INVADE LAKE TAHOE HOMES AS BREAK-INS SURGE AND LOCALS FORTIFY DEFENSES

As more and more people flock to the Sunshine State from other states and countries, the cities keep developing further and further inland, and in the southern part of the state, that means developing on top of the Everglades.

The more this happens, the more we will see videos of our friend here running scared through the streets of the suburbs, which could be dangerous for both the bears and the human population.

Here's hoping Mr. Ursus Americanus Floridanus made it back to the 'Glades in one piece and that no one was seriously injured.

item.title: Team USA withdraws from FIFA U-17 World Cup amid State Department travel warning in Middle East
item.description: U.S. Soccer pulled its U-17 men's team from the FIFA World Cup in Qatar, citing a State Department Level 3 travel advisory over armed conflict risks.
item.content:encoded:
U.S. Soccer withdrew its under-17 men’s national team from the upcoming World Cup in Qatar on Wednesday, citing safety concerns and a State Department warning about the risk of armed conflict, per multiple reports.

The federation notified players in a letter that it was canceling both its pre-tournament camp and participation in the competition, pointing to the government’s Level 3 travel advisory and related directives affecting embassy staff and families.

"The well-being of our players and staff will always be our top priority," the letter said.

The decision comes eight days before the tournament’s scheduled Nov. 19 kickoff. FIFA has scheduled the competition to run through Dec. 13.

The State Department’s Oct. 23 advisory urges Americans to reconsider travel to Qatar because of the risk of armed conflict. U.S. government employees must obtain special authorization to travel there.

DEADLY SECURITY RISKS PROMPT UPDATED TRAVEL WARNINGS FOR 13 COUNTRIES

The advisory cites attacks by Iranian-backed Houthi forces against civilian airports and other infrastructure in neighboring Saudi Arabia, warning that the hostilities could spread rapidly beyond the immediate area.

It also identifies risks to civilian aviation from regional political and military tensions. Americans who travel to Qatar are urged to prepare to shelter in place and have an emergency departure plan that does not depend on U.S. government assistance.

Fox News Digital previously reported that an Iranian missile struck Qatar’s Al-Udeid Air Base in March. Qatari officials reported no injuries.

Fox News Digital also reported that nonemergency U.S. government employees and their families were ordered out of Saudi Arabia on Oct. 23 over safety concerns.

STATE DEPARTMENT ISSUES TRAVEL ADVISORY AS ARRESTS AND EXIT BANS HIT POPULAR DESTINATION

For the American players, the withdrawal ends a World Cup opportunity less than a week after head coach Alex Aldaz announced his 21-player roster Nov. 6.

The Americans were scheduled to open against Montenegro on Nov. 21, face Chile on Nov. 24 and finish Group J play against Algeria on Nov. 27.

The roster included Philadelphia Union forward Malik Jakupovic, who scored eight goals during qualifying, and players affiliated with European clubs including AC Milan, Ajax and PSV.

The United States earned its place in February, winning its qualifying group in St. Vincent and the Grenadines. The Americans beat the hosts 8-0 and St. Kitts and Nevis 10-0 before clinching qualification with a 1-1 draw against the Dominican Republic.

Nine members of that qualifying squad were included on the World Cup roster.

This year’s competition is the second under the tournament’s expanded annual, 48-team format and the second of five consecutive editions awarded to Qatar.

FIFA published the tournament’s official squad lists Wednesday, outlining plans for 104 matches and a final at Ahmad bin Ali Stadium.

item.title: Hakeem Jeffries faces progressive holdouts but no rival as House speaker race takes shape
item.description: New members of Congress in "The Bloc" say they're undecided on Hakeem Jeffries for House speaker, pressing for legislative guarantees before January.
item.content:encoded:
Familiar faces populate the 110-plus new members of Congress.

A few "freshmen" are returning to the House. Even if they’ve been gone for a while.

There’s Rep.-elect Hilda Solis, D-Calif., who last served in Congress in 2009. She departed to become President Obama’s labor secretary.

Rep.-elect Jerry Carl, R-Ala., just left Capitol Hill early last year after losing a primary to Rep. Barry Moore, R-Ala., who is now moving to the Senate. 

REPORTER’S NOTEBOOK: A DEMOCRATIC MAJORITY COULD EXPOSE THE LIMITS OF THE PROGRESSIVE AGENDA

And then there’s Rep.-elect Melissa Bean, D-Ill. She first won a seat in the House in 2004 and lost in 2010. Now, Bean is back.

Her advice to the rookies?

"Make sure you get a really good scheduler and that they schedule eating because your staff will run you all day long," Bean said. "You're kind of like the football that they pass from one staff member to the other. The whole day goes by, and you’re starving."

House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries, D-N.Y., is on track to become House speaker in January. But some progressives are holding out. Bean was a moderate when she served before. Yours truly asked about the natural unease between left-wing Democrats and centrists.

"It’s a pretty united majority," replied Bean.

"Do you think that’s overstated tension?" I followed up.

"I think it always is," Bean answered. "But that’s a media thing, right?"

So to recap for new members: Get a good scheduler? Check. Make sure you have time to eat? Check. And, blame the press.

Ha.

MEET THE FAR-LEFT INSURGENTS WAGING WAR ON THE DEMOCRATIC ESTABLISHMENT IN 2026 MIDTERMS

But, seriously, there are some progressives who aren’t willing to publicly commit to supporting Jeffries as speaker. Most of these incoming members comprise what’s now known as "The Bloc." It’s kind of like "The Squad" some years ago.

And they’re not tipping their hand about Jeffries.

They’re trying to squeeze the New York Democrat and others for legislative guarantees.

"We're not withholding votes. What we're doing is saying we're undecided. We're not going to rubber-stamp anything," said Rep.-elect Adam Hamawy, D-N.J.

"I don't think it's about the individual. It’s about the agenda and the agenda that actually reflects the priorities of the American people," said Rep.-elect Melat Kiros, D-Colo. "It's about what kind of priorities, what kind of floor votes, what kind of plan do we have to actually fight for the bold change the American people sent us here to do."

"I think we need to be talking about improving the lives of working people and helping them join unions," said Rep.-elect Claire Valdez, D-N.Y.

There’s nothing groundbreaking going on here. Progressive Democrats won. Democrats won big. The Bloc wants to flex its muscles and execute its agenda.

Otherwise, those members have explaining to do with their base. Thus, it’s not that extraordinary to have a group of members not automatically supporting someone for a leadership post.

They’re playing the political game to get the best deal for the people they represent. They can’t just back Jeffries out of the gate. They must first extract a concession.

Rep. Joe Courtney, D-Conn., witnessed these machinations before when former House Speaker Nancy Pelosi, D-Calif., tried to manage dissent about her leadership after elections.

"I actually think it's a weaker version [of protest] this time," said Courtney. "I think [Jeffries] did a great job of keeping the caucus really marching in the same direction in the last two years. Which was not easy."

"There's no question that as a management matter, having a bigger majority is a lot easier than having a tiny majority. That's just basic math," said Rep. Jim Himes, D-Conn. 

"As a new speaker, he's going to need to do a lot of work to make sure he is listening to everybody and managing. So, it's going to be a lot easier than if it had been a four-vote majority. But managing Democrats is always a challenge."

So, for all of the talk about "issues" progressives may have with Jeffries, they’re not offering up an alternative name for speaker. And, frankly, no one could beat Jeffries in this environment.

PROGRESSIVES FUME AT HAKEEM JEFFRIES FOR SAYING DEMOCRATS WON'T 'GET EVEN' WITH TRUMP

"You can’t beat somebody with nobody. And that’s kind of where I think this ‘race’ stands," said Courtney, putting "race" in air quotes. "The worst thing that could happen is to start this Congress off like it happened in 2023, where we went through 15 ballots (before electing a speaker)."

That’s a reference to House Republicans stymieing the election of former House Speaker Kevin McCarthy, R-Calif.

Rep. Glenn Ivey, D-Md., appeared mystified at progressive machinations over Jeffries.

"It is kind of odd. You get a coach who takes his team to the Super Bowl. They win by 30 points, and then they got folks who want to fire him the next day. It's a little hard to figure out," said Ivey.

Progressives may express concerns about Jeffries. But remember that Democrats have the majority because they flipped deeply red districts. The Democrats who will represent those districts know that voters could note if they supported Jeffries — or broke with him.

Rep.-elect Don Leonard, D-Ohio, appears to be one of the most outspoken incoming members. Leonard emerged from nowhere to defeat Rep. Mike Carey, R-Ohio. On Instagram, Leonard said Democratic leaders informed him in "no uncertain terms" that if he didn’t support Jeffries, the party brass would make his "life a living hell" and assure he would lose re-election.

So, there are questions from the left and questions from centrists.

Yours truly pressed Jeffries about whether the skepticism from progressives was real or just politics as they try to extract legislative promises out of him.

"I'm going to work hard to talk to every single member about what we've been able to do together over the last two years and what the opportunities are for us to do together in the next two years, to deliver upon the dramatic change that the American people so decisively voted for this past Tuesday," Jeffries replied, not directly answering.

"That sounds like you don't have it nailed down. Is that right?" I followed up.

Jeffries chuckled.

"You think I don't have the vote nailed down?" he countered.

"I'm asking you. You're the vote counter. Do you have them? Yes or no?" I queried.

"I guess we'll find out next Wednesday," Jeffries said.

I have reported on the air that it would take a lot to sidetrack a prospective Jeffries speakership.

House Democrats will likely have north of 260 seats in the new Congress.

The magic number to claim the gavel on the House floor is 218. It’s hard to see Jeffries losing 42 votes. Especially when no one is competing against him. Moreover, he only needs to marshal 131 votes in the Democratic Caucus (just better than half of 260) to become the official nominee.

But that said, there is tension in the Democratic ranks.

Some of that is natural inside such a massive coalition. It’s not construed by the press corps.

The question is how will Jeffries manage those disparate factions when he clasps the gavel as speaker Jan. 3.

The dispute now is a symptom of what problems could lie ahead.

item.title: Rachel Maddow welcomes 'big fight' between socialist and moderate Democrats after midterm wins
item.description: MS NOW host Rachel Maddow told "The View" she hopes moderate Democrats and democratic socialists have a "big fight" that strengthens the party's big tent.
item.content:encoded:
MS NOW host Rachel Maddow told ABC's "The View" Wednesday she hopes there will be a "big fight" between moderate and socialist members of the Democratic Party in Congress.

While promoting her new book "Department of Fate," Maddow discussed recent calls from some progressive senators to replace Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer, D-N.Y., once Democrats take control of the Senate in January.

Those calling for new leadership included Democratic senators-elect Adam Hamilton of Kansas, Troy Jackson of Maine and Abdul El-Sayed of Michigan.

SCHUMER FACES MUTINY FROM NEWLY ELECTED SENATE DEMS AS PARTY PREPARES TO SEIZE POWER

Though some Democrats have expressed concerns about infighting within the party, Maddow dismissed those concerns and welcomed the idea of moderate Democrats debating socialists.

"I feel like the Democrats have kind of first-world problems right now," Maddow joked. "There was so much talk ahead of the election about, ‘Oh there’s these handful of democratic socialist-associated candidates. How are the Democrats going to do?’ 

"Well, the Democrats elected so many people. Yes, they elected a handful of democratic socialists, but also the Blue Dog coalition, which is the conservative Democrats. They have like a dozen new members too."

Maddow argued that the Democratic Party now includes members with a wide range of political views and that debate could strengthen the party.

"I think that it’s righteous for them to have a big fight. I hope they don’t settle it instantly. I hope they actually do have a debate. I think competition makes us stronger," she said.

Fox News Digital reached out to Schumer's office for comment but did not immediately receive a response.

BILL MAHER WARNS DEMOCRATS THAT SOME ON FAR LEFT WANT 'COMMUNISM' AFTER MIDTERM SWEEP

Maddow's comments came one day after "The View" co-host Whoopi Goldberg called out congressional Democrats publicly debating whether to replace Schumer and House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries, D-N.Y., as party leaders.

"This is my two cents," Goldberg said. "I don’t want to hear this from you right now. I want to know what all of you are, all of you Democrats, what are your plans for the first 100 days? I don’t care if you’ve been there forever or just got there. What are your plans?

"We put you in there to clean house, to make sure that the government works the way the people want it to work," she added. "I don’t want to hear all this infighting, because then you become the distraction, and then you become no better than the Republicans were. So, just get your stuff together. All of you."

MADDOW FEARS TRUMP MIGRANT DETENTION CENTERS MAY BE USED TO IMPRISON ‘THE REST OF US’

Democratic strategist and pollster Doug Schoen disagreed with Maddow's assessment.

"It’s clear the Dems won an overwhelming victory because of moderates, not progressives. The American people are demanding action on the affordability crisis, not intraparty infighting between progressives and moderates," Schoen told Fox News Digital.
